Lesson 077: architecture interview questions

    What this shows

    Questions are part of the answer

    A design question is vague on purpose. The interviewer is listening for whether you find the real problem before solving one.

    Details first eats the clock

    Start with the classes and you never reach the parts that show architecture: trade-offs, failures and how you'd know it works.

    Say the trade-off out loud

    Two options, one choice and the reason is the most architect-like sentence you can say in an interview.

    This lab is a model, not a real hiring rubric. It uses Lesson 077's scorecard: five things scored 0 to 4. Requirements: 4 if you ask first. Numbers: 4 if you estimate after asking, 2 if you estimate without asking (the numbers describe the wrong game). Design: 4 for boxes then zoom, 2 for details first. Trade-offs: 4 for two options and a reason, 1 for boxes without them. Failures and measurement: 4 if you reach them. Time: questions 5 min, numbers 3, boxes and zoom 12, trade-offs 5, closing 5. Details first takes all the time that's left, so anything after it isn't reached. Real interviews vary; the shape of a good answer doesn't.
